status: Academic full-stack project / locally runnable Python Flask application
oneLineSummary: A role-based Flask internship portal that connects students, employers, and administrators through secure application, review, and account-management workflows.

summary.systemDefinition: A web-based internship management platform built for a fictitious early-career recruitment start-up, BrightPath Careers, to centralise internship discovery, application handling, and platform administration.
coreWorkflowsFeatures: Secure login with Student, Employer, and Admin roles
Student workflows for browsing internships, applying, uploading resumes, reviewing submitted applications, and updating profiles
Employer workflows for viewing internship listings, reviewing applicants, reading cover letters, and updating application outcomes with feedback
Admin workflows for viewing platform activity, managing user accounts, and updating account status
Bootstrap-based multi-page interface with role-specific views and navigation
Support for profile images, employer logos, and PDF resume uploads
Local database bootstrap with seed data for development and demonstration
summary.businessOrOperationalImpact: The system reduces friction between students seeking relevant internship opportunities and employers needing a simple workflow to review applicants and manage hiring decisions in one place.
summary.engineeringValue: The project demonstrates practical full-stack web engineering with Flask routing, session-based authentication, role-based access control, relational database design, file upload handling, password hashing, template-driven UI integration, and environment-aware local setup.

projectNarrative.problem: Students often struggle to find and track relevant internship opportunities, while smaller employers lack a centralised system for posting roles, reviewing applicants, and managing decisions consistently.
projectNarrative.approach: I built a Python Flask application with separate student, employer, and admin experiences, integrated relational database models, Bootstrap templates, JavaScript-enhanced page interactions, secure login with hashed passwords, and a local-first runtime setup that can run with SQLite while preserving MySQL compatibility.
projectNarrative.result: The project delivered a structured internship management system with clear role-specific workflows, secure authentication, application tracking, profile management, and a reproducible database-backed local development environment.

engineeringHighlights: Role-based access control for Student, Employer, and Admin users
Session-based authentication and route protection with Flask
Relational schema covering users, students, employers, internships, and applications
Student application workflow with PDF resume upload and cover letter submission
Employer review workflow with application status updates and feedback
Admin user-management workflow with account status controls
Bootstrap and JavaScript frontend integrated with Flask templates and server-rendered data
SQLite local bootstrap with seed users for demo/testing, while retaining MySQL-oriented compatibility
Smoke-test coverage for login, profile, application, employer, and admin pages

reflection.tradeoffs: The main trade-off was balancing assignment simplicity with maintainability. The project stayed within a lightweight Flask and server-rendered architecture instead of adding heavier abstractions such as SQLAlchemy or a frontend framework, which kept it aligned with coursework constraints while still supporting secure authentication, role-specific workflows, and database-backed functionality.
lessonsLearned: Role-based systems need explicit access checks and consistent session handling from the start.
Frontend templates and backend query fields must evolve together; mismatches quickly break real pages.
A reproducible local database setup is as important as the live schema because it determines whether the project can actually be demonstrated and maintained.
File uploads require both UX considerations and backend safeguards around paths, formats, and defaults.
Even academic systems benefit from lightweight automated smoke tests to catch broken routes, missing assets, and integration regressions early.
futureImprovements: Add full automated tests for access control, application status transitions, and file upload paths
Allow employers to create and edit internship postings through the UI
Add richer admin analytics and internship activity dashboards
Introduce email notifications for application updates and account changes
Improve validation, audit history, and feedback visibility across workflows
Refine the data layer with migrations and cleaner environment-specific configuration
